title: Cipher Maps: Total Functions as Trapdoor Approximations
description: Proposes the cipher map abstraction as a unifying framework for parameterized-leakage outsourced function evaluation in the quantitative information flow (QIF) tradition. Characterizes value-side security through four measurable properties (totality, representation-uniformity delta, correctness eta, composability) parameterized by (eta, epsilon, delta, mu). The acceptance-predicate apparatus exposes a Pareto frontier between expected codeword length L and TV-leakage: under integer codeword constraints, the Shannon-optimal corner (L = -log_2 epsilon + H(Y)) and the TV-optimal corner are distinct (42x TV reduction at 17% length overhead on heavy-tailed value distributions). A multi-instance composition theorem (the coincidence oracle: accuracy(t) = 1 - 1/2 sum_y alpha(y)^t) gives a closed form for shared-f multi-instance leakage; randomized encoding (multiplicity K(x) > 1) is the deployment-side defense. The framework subsumes Bloom filters, frequency-hiding encryption, and encrypted Boolean search as instances. Empirical validation on the 20 Newsgroups corpus plus a controlled membership-inference study. Quantitative confidentiality grounded in the entropy ratio framework developed in companion work (towell2026maxconf).
